title: Brass Sleeve Bushing – Thermal Contraction for Interference-Fit Installation

summary: Determine the cooling temperature required to contract a brass sleeve bushing enough for clearance during installation into a steel housing.

problemStatement:
A maintenance engineer must install a replacement brass sleeve bushing into an existing steel housing. At room temperature, the bushing outside diameter is intentionally slightly larger than the housing bore, creating an interference fit after assembly. For installation, only the bushing is cooled so thermal contraction temporarily reduces its outside diameter enough to provide a specified diametral clearance; the steel housing remains at room temperature.

The industry image is representative only. Its product dimensions and material condition are not analytical inputs. The assigned coefficient of thermal expansion is a representative published value for C26000 cartridge brass; the remaining dimensions and initial temperature are instructor-assigned teaching values.
engineeringGoal: Determine the room-temperature interference, required cooled diameter, necessary temperature change, and final bushing temperature for installation. Interpret the signs and assess the simplified uniform thermal-contraction model without extending the analysis to press-fit contact stresses.
